scope: Cross-research-session delivery and recovery for a project-scoped research stream. The durable per-task event log plus the current snapshot are the recovery basis; a chat/DSH WebSocket message is never authority.

authority.business_authority: B CAS stores (task/approval/budget) remain authoritative; the event log is a replayable projection.
authority.research_record_authority: C owns the ResearchRecord question/proposal/round/task references; B never writes them.
authority.session_authority: A chat/DSH session id is a client identity only. It carries a cursor and can never set project scope or business state.
authority.snapshot_rule: replay(cursor) delivers durable facts after the cursor; reset=true additionally delivers the full current snapshot, which the consumer uses to rebuild the projection.

identity_rules.event_id: stable, non-empty; the dedup identity of one fact
identity_rules.dedup_key: stable across retries/restarts/outbox redelivery; equal dedup_key is a no-op
identity_rules.seq: per-owner monotonic integer; a regression is a corrupt stream and is rejected
identity_rules.revision: monotonic business-projection revision per task/attempt; a stale revision is ignored
identity_rules.task_id: the owning task; an event for another task never enters this projection
identity_rules.attempt: the execution attempt; an older attempt is stale and a newer attempt requires its own projection
identity_rules.project_id: server-resolved project scope; a fact for another project is rejected
identity_rules.payload_version: integer version of the event payload; a newer version is not consumed
identity_rules.owner: B (task/approval/budget state) or C (reference-only research facts)

business_state_ownership.double_write_rule: neither side writes the other side's business state; C reference facts never mutate B status, and B rejects a C fact that carries B state

cursor.consumer_rule: treat the cursor as an opaque token; never parse it, never derive authority from it
cursor.expiry_rule: a cursor whose issued_at is older than max_age_s is expired; replay returns reset=true with reason cursor_expired

snapshot.content: every durable event for this owner in sequence order
snapshot.rule: reset is always explicit (reset=true + reason + snapshot); a lost cursor is never an empty-but-silent success

expiry_reset.action: discard the cursor, rebuild the projection from the snapshot, then reconcile idempotently
expiry_reset.duplicate_dispatch: forbidden; the action ledger returns replay for the same idempotency key

task_attempt_revision.attempt_rule: an event from an older attempt is stale; an event from a different newer attempt requires a new projection and is never mixed
task_attempt_revision.revision_rule: apply only revision > projection.revision; equal-revision additive facts are accepted; equal-revision status facts are out_of_order
task_attempt_revision.out_of_order_rule: a lower revision never overwrites a newer projection; the event is recorded as stale and has no effect

project_scope.source: server-resolved project id, never a chat session or a client payload
project_scope.rule: append and replay reject an event whose project_id differs from the stream's project scope
project_scope.cross_project: a cursor from another project/principal is refused, not reinterpreted

rules.replay: cursor-addressed durable replay plus the current snapshot; WebSocket/live messages are notifications only, never authority. A fresh subscriber may start from cursor=0 and read the durable log.
rules.out_of_order: events are applied in durable seq order; a lower business revision is stale and ignored; an equal-revision status fact is out_of_order and cannot change status; a newer non-terminal fact cannot revive a terminal projection.
rules.duplicate: equal event_id or dedup_key is a no-op; the durable log appends nothing and the projection reports duplicate.
rules.idempotent_consumer: the consumer applies facts idempotently, and every externally visible action (approval request, submit, dispatch) is claimed through the persistent (action, idempotency_key) ledger; a replay returns the original TaskRef and never dispatches twice.
rules.terminal_projection: once a task/approval/budget target is terminal, its terminal state is write-once for that projection: a stale or newer status event cannot overwrite it. Additive facts (task_ref/submit reference) may still be attached.
rules.revocation: authorization is re-evaluated on the live stream; a revocation closes delivery immediately, the next poll returns reset=true with permission_changed and no events, and new connections are refused. A cursor does not preserve permission.
rules.rph_exit_after_task_completion: an RPH/session exit is not a task cancellation. If the task is terminal the session stops immediately (no LLM wait, no new dispatch); if non-terminal the task continues and the consumer returns without blocking, re-reading the cursor/snapshot on reattach.
rules.lost_cursor: a missing, invalid, ahead-of-tail, expired or retention-gap cursor forces an explicit snapshot reset; the consumer rebuilds projection state and reconciles actions through the idempotency ledger, so a lost cursor cannot cause a duplicate submit or dispatch.
rules.session_is_not_authority: a chat/DSH session id, its claimed project id and any temporary server message are never project authority; only the durable projection and the verified server scope decide the project.
rules.stale_event: a stale event cannot overwrite a terminal projection or a newer revision; it is recorded as stale/out_of_order/terminal_protected with no state change.

steps: if missing/invalid/expired/ahead/retention-gap: discard it and rebuild from the snapshot
otherwise replay durable events after the cursor
apply events idempotently in seq order (duplicate/stale/out-of-order/terminal-protected are no-ops)
decide the next action from the authoritative projection
claim any approval/submit action through the persistent idempotency ledger
publish the committed action fact with a stable dedup key
recovery.no_duplicate_dispatch: a reset rebuilds submitted/terminal state from the snapshot, and the ledger's committed row returns the original TaskRef; no second submit is created
recovery.cross_process: the cursor is a durable seq + issue time, so a new process resumes from the same log without a live client

session_lifecycle.attach: a session provides a cursor only; the server resolves project/task/attempt
session_lifecycle.detach: recording a detached session never changes task/approval/budget state
session_lifecycle.reconnect: replay from the last cursor; on reset rebuild from the snapshot

compatibility.legacy_event_log: old records without the _research payload block remain readable (task_id=owner_id, attempt=1, revision=seq, owner=B)
compatibility.legacy_cursor: the integer after_seq remains valid for the legacy SSE endpoint; the research cursor is an additive opaque token

digest_rule: sha256 of canonical compact JSON (sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=False) with this field set to the empty string
